newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa futures end at seven-month low.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa futures end at seven-month low.

text.p: Benchmark London cocoa futures slipped out of their range and closed at a seven-month low of 972 stg a tonne basis March on Thursday as selling intensified in late session, traders said.
The March contract tumbled past the technically-sensitive 975 level -- the bottom end of a two-month range -- and touched a session low of 970 stg. At the close, losses totalled 17 stg.
Traders said late selling which wiped the last five stg off the market was technically-inspired and could have come from trade-related long liqidation or belated hedging.
"London was looking very weak. There was left-over long liquidation. New York stops were triggered and that started the liquidation process," said one trader.
March cocoa had been browsing comfortably between 975 and 1,025 stg in the last two months, bouncing each time it touched the low end of the range amid a dearth of news on the fundamental front.
News that Ivory Coast opened its cocoa season and kept the farm-gate price at an unchanged 350 CFA francs a kg, which the market had been awaiting for weeks, was brushed aside.
"The market is just ignoring all the news. It's lost its way," said one trader.
Industry buyers stepped back completely, leaving the market devoid of any incentive to pursue the upside, traders said.

Traders are likely to keep a close tab on Ivorian arrivals in the coming weeks to gauge the size of the current harvest but initial crops may not be indicative. "I don't know if this market will be fundamentally dictated or not," said one.
At the close, the front-month December contract stood 18 stg lower on the day at 943 stg a tonne with further forward contracts shedding between nine and 16 stg.
Turnover reached 5,292 lots, in line with recent levels.
Chartists say March is likely to head for support now pegged at the March low of 955 stg a tonne.
